# CLI commands

Use the checkout entry `node bin/mobile-inspector.mjs` when no executable is installed on PATH. All examples use placeholder selectors obtained from your own running owner; they are not literal IDs.

## Current command inventory

Version 0.1.0 · development

```text
Mobile Inspector 0.1.0
Usage: mobile-inspector <command>

  help                 Show available commands
  --version            Show installed version
  doctor [--json]      Check local prerequisites and capabilities
  start [server flags] Start or reuse the managed local viewer
  instance status      Inspect the active owner
  project              Register, list or configure local projects
  demo --project ID    Create a labelled synthetic recording
  query TOOL --project ID  Read scoped capture summaries
  incidents            Browse bounded incident evidence
  watch --project ID   Foreground diagnosis lease; --off stops it
  diagnose --project ID --incident ID --generation GEN
  mcp serve/setup/remove   Project-scoped evidence bridge and Codex setup

Run start --help for connection and certificate options.
```

## Read before mutating

Help and version paths do not start a collector. `doctor --json` distinguishes discovered prerequisites from operational capabilities. Start the foreground owner explicitly before project mutations, demo, queries or MCP operations. All commands accept `--home PATH`; use the same tool-owned home for one instance.

`project add` grants a selected trusted Git root local project authority. `project build` maps app/platform/environment/build to an existing commit and contained source root. App-reported paths do not grant access. `demo --project ID` creates host-labelled synthetic records without business requests.

## Query selectors

Call `query list_sessions --project ID`, then retain session ID and generation for trace/log requests. Default limit is 50, maximum 200. Continue `nextCursor` only with unchanged scope/selectors/limit. Stale generations and cursors fail; do not silently restart in another recording. Summary is default, and partial results expose gaps.

`watch` and `diagnose` are explicit foreground orchestration commands, not guarantees of model availability. Review [diagnosis limitations](diagnosis.md). Stop your own foreground process with Ctrl+C; never kill an arbitrary PID based on a port or stale lock.
